ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There is a central node in the circuit diagram. The left branch from P to the central node is a current source labeled 2 A, with the arrow pointing to the right, therefore injecting 2 A current into the central node. The upper branch from Q is connected to the central node through a 5 Ω resistor, and the resistor voltage V_R is labeled with the upper end positive and the central-node side negative. The right branch goes from the central node through a 1 F capacitor to R, and the capacitor voltage V_C is labeled with the left end positive and the right end negative, therefore according to the passive sign convention the capacitor current flows out from the central node to the right. The lower branch goes from the central node through a 2 H inductor to S, and the inductor voltage V_L is labeled with the upper end positive and the lower end negative, therefore according to the passive sign convention the inductor current flows out from the central node downward. Reasoning: Given V_R = 5 V and the resistor is 5 Ω, so the resistor current i_R = V_R/R = 5/5 = 1 A, with direction from the positive end of the resistor to the negative end, namely flowing downward into the central node. Given V_C = 4 sin 2t and capacitance C = 1 F, so the capacitor current flowing out of the central node is i_C = C dV_C/dt = 1·d(4 sin 2t)/dt = 8 cos 2t. Write KCL for the central node: the entering currents are the 2 A current source plus the 1 A resistor current, and the leaving currents are i_C and i_L, therefore 2 + 1 = i_C + i_L. Thus i_L = 3 - 8 cos 2t. The inductor L = 2 H, and the polarity of V_L is consistent with the passive sign convention of i_L, so V_L = L di_L/dt = 2·d(3 - 8 cos 2t)/dt = 2·16 sin 2t = 32 sin 2t V.
